title: Apollo 12 - CSM Yankee Clipper, LM Intrepid
_comment: Apollo 12, the pinpoint landing: Intrepid came down in the Ocean of Storms 535 ft from Surveyor III, the landing site updated in powered descent by the ground's noun 69, after a hybrid translunar trajectory off the free return and a lunar orbit 14.6 deg to the equator. Sources: the Apollo 12 Mission Report (MSC-01855), its trajectory reconstruction and guidance supplements, the Saturn V flight evaluation report for AS-507 (MPR-SAT-FE-70-1), the final flight plan, the Apollo Flight Journal's and the Apollo Lunar Surface Journal's transcripts, and LROC's maps of the site. Distances in km, times in GET seconds or hhh:mm:ss (GET counts from range zero, 16:22:00 UTC on 14 November 1969).

call_signs._comment: The call signs CAPCOM used for the flight and its vehicles, Intrepid on the surface as well (Apollo Lunar Surface Journal) [published]; CAPCOM's own calls on the timeline say 12, Clipper and Intrepid where he did

start_calls.translunar_coast: {mission}, Houston. Good TLI. You're on the free return; MCC-2 will put you on the hybrid.
start_calls.lunar_orbit: {mission}, Houston. You're in a 66 by 54-mile orbit with {lm} docked. GO for undocking comes on the thirteenth rev.
start_calls.lunar_descent: {lm}, Houston. You're on the descent orbit. Your state vector and GO for PDI are coming, and a Noun 69 after throttle-up.
start_calls.lunar_surface: {lm_landed}, Houston. You're STAY. {csm}'s plane change comes first; the ascent PAD at {ascent_pad}.
start_calls.lunar_ascent: {lm}, Houston. Your ascent PAD is in: liftoff at {liftoff}. P12 when you're ready.
start_calls.tei: {csm}, Houston. The LM is gone and the photography plane change is done; your TEI PAD is on its way up.
start_calls.transearth_coast: Houston: TEI was good. Your midcourse PADs will come up to trim the entry corridor.
start_calls.entry: Houston: entry interface in about twenty minutes. P61, CM/SM SEP when P62 asks, ELS LOGIC and AUTO.
start_calls._comment: CAPCOM's word as each start phase begins, the simulator's own [adapted]

vehicles._comment: Apollo 12's vehicles where they differ from data/spacecraft.json's, Apollo 11's

mass._source: The mission report's mass properties (MSC-01855, Table A-I: the CSM 63,535.6 lb at transposition and docking, the CM 12,283.5 lb after CM/SM separation; the LM 33,586.9 lb at launch and 33,985.5 lb at its separation, 10,749.6 lb at lunar lift-off and 16,564.2 lb at landing) and propellant loads (sections 7.11 and 8.13: the SPS's 40,817 lb, the SM RCS's 1,341 lb, the CM RCS's 208.4 lb; the DPS's 18,429 lb, 1,175 lb left at its cutoff; the APS's 5,236 lb; the LM RCS's 634 lb) [published]; the vehicle at the S-IVB's second ignition, 134,986 kg (297,593 lb: the AS-507 flight evaluation report, Table 17-10) [published]. From them [derived]: the CM dry of its RCS's propellant, the SM dry of its own and the SPS's; the ascent stage dry, with the crew and their equipment, at lift-off less its APS load and the RCS's 459 lb left then [estimated: the 634 lb less the 315 lb used to docking, less the 140 lb the ascent and the rendezvous took]; the descent stage dry, the LM at its separation less the rest, which puts the LM at landing within 8 lb of its 16,564.2 [simplified: the LM carries its crew from TLI, 399 lb more than its 33,586.9 lb at launch]; the S-IVB dry with the Instrument Unit, the adapter and the residuals, the vehicle at ignition less the CSM, the LM and the propellant

sps._source: The SPS's load, 40,817 lb (MSC-01855, section 7.11.1) [published]; its engine Apollo 11's

sm_rcs._source: The SM RCS's load, 1,341 lb in four quads (MSC-01855, section 7.11.2) [published]

cm_rcs._source: The CM RCS's usable load, 208.4 lb in two systems (MSC-01855, section 7.11.2) [published]

dps._source: The DPS's load, 18,429 lb (MSC-01855, section 8.13.1) [published]; its engine Apollo 11's

aps._source: The APS's load, 5,236 lb (MSC-01855, section 8.13.2) [published]; its engine Apollo 11's, as the flight's was predicted to within 1 % (3,495 to 3,460 lbf, 309.5 s: ibid., Table 8.9-I)

lm_rcs._source: The LM RCS's load, 317 lb in each of its two systems (MSC-01855, section 8.13.3) [published]

sivb._source: The J-2 in AS-507's second S-IVB burn, TLI: 341.2 s from 134,986 kg at ignition to 63,340 kg at the cutoff signal (MPR-SAT-FE-70-1, section 7.8 and Table 17-10), with LOX depletion 10.14 s after the cutoff (section 7.9) [published]; its specific impulse at the steady-state slice, 429.2 s (Table 7-2) [published]; the thrust the burn's mean flow gives at that specific impulse, and the propellant to depletion [derived; the thrust and the specific impulse held through the burn: simplified]

ascent_guidance._source: Insertion climbing at 37.0 ft/s, the ascent PAD's N76 (Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, 140:19:25) [published]

parking_orbit._comment: Apollo 12's orbit at insertion, from the Saturn V flight evaluation report for AS-507 (MPR-SAT-FE-70-1, Table 4-5): inclination 32.540 deg and descending node 123.126 deg east of the launch meridian at range zero, insertion at 703.91 s at 32.682 N 51.131 W, 190.9 km [published], put in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. The report's 185.4 x 181.2 km orbit is taken as circular [simplified]. The launch isn't flown for Apollo 12 yet: it would want AS-507's stages, and its lightning strikes

launch_refsmmat._comment: The launch pad REFSMMAT, the orientation the CMC's IMU was released at liftoff: X horizontal along the flight azimuth (72.029 deg, MPR-SAT-FE-70-1, section 4.1), Z down along Launch Complex 39A's vertical, Y = Z x X, each a stable member axis in the ICRF, from tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. The parking_orbit and translunar_coast start phases start aligned to it

tli._comment: TLI's conic, as the flown TLI left the stack on it: C3 -1,834,425 m2/s2 and eccentricity 0.96966, in the plane of inclination 30.355 deg and descending node 120.338 deg (MPR-SAT-FE-70-1, Table 4-6: at TLI, 10 s after the cutoff signal) [published]; the plane in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]; the TLI perigee's place in the burn, which starts it at the flown 2:47:22.7 [derived]. The RTCC plans TLI's ignition time and energy (Rtcc.plan_tli()) for the free return the flown TLI left the stack on, past the Moon 280.2 nmi up at 83:44:04.4, 29.73 S 169.11 E (MSC-01855, Table 5-IV) [published]. The midcourse corrections then aim at pericynthion_alt_km at pericynthion_get, the pericynthion in the plane of the lunar orbit over the landing site (node_targeting), where Apollo 12's MCC-2 left it: 65.1 nmi at 83:28:38.8, 0.71 N 161.968 E (ibid.) [published], 0.13 deg from that plane [derived]. It was the hybrid, off the free return, from which LOI-1 turned the orbit's plane 6 deg into that one (its PAD's 603.6 ft/s out of the plane). earliest_get_s: 2:20:00, ahead of the S-IVB's restart preparation [estimated]

loi._comment: LOI-1's targets: the flight plan's 168.9 by 58.7 nmi (Table 1-5; flown 168.8 by 62.6 nmi, MSC-01855, Table 5-VI) at the final PAD's TIG, 83:25:18.51 (Apollo Flight Journal, 80:50:55) [published], above the Moon's mean radius [simplified]. The RTCC solves the burn at that TIG (Rtcc.plan_loi()), the orbit's plane over the landing site

doi._comment: Descent orbit insertion: the LM's pericynthion 8.3 nmi above the landing site, where powered descent begins, the DOI PAD's N42 (Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, 108:00:32) [published], on the pass that lands at the landing time

landing._comment: Apollo 12's landing site: the targeted point was set on Surveyor III (MSC-01855, section 4.3), which LROC's images put at 3.0162 S, 23.4180 W; Intrepid came down 535 ft from it (ibid.), at 3.0128 S, 23.4219 W by LROC's (Wagner et al., 2017), at 110:32:36.2 (ibid., Table 5-III) [published]. The site's height is the terrain's there (data/terrain/, LROC's model of the site: 1,432 m below the reference sphere). The lunar orbit crossed the site heading 284.2 deg, 14.6 deg to the lunar equator (the trajectory reconstruction's -14.57 deg; the ground track from PDI at 6.76 S 7.82 W to the landing, ibid.) [derived]. The lunar_surface and lunar_ascent start phases set Intrepid down where it came down, with the DPS's 1,175 lb left at its cutoff (ibid., section 8.13.1) [published]

pdi._comment: The LM state vector the ground uplinks with the PDI PAD is off by this much at PDI, in LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down): 4,400 ft along the track, which the Doppler residuals showed after DOI (MSC-01855, section 4.2) [published], and 40 m low [estimated: what gives the landing radar's first delta-H as the crew read it, minus 918 and minus 1,000 ft (Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, 110:24:12)]. Powered descent's landing site correction (N69) is MSFN's powered flight processor's reading of the error along the track, off by n69_sigma_m [estimated: it read 4,200 ft where the residuals had shown 4,400]

ascent._comment: The RTCC times the liftoff for the CSM to lead the LM by this angle at insertion [estimated, as Apollo 11's]. The CSM's first plane change puts its orbit over the LM at the planned liftoff (the flight plan's, Table 1-6) [published]

rendezvous._comment: The coelliptic sequence after the insertion: CSI at the LM's first apolune; TPI 2 h 27 min 9 s after the insertion's cutoff, the CSI PAD's N37 (144:38:00, Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, 140:21:36; the ascent burned 423.2 s from 142:03:47.8, MSC-01855, Table 5-VI), flown at 144:36:26; the midcourse corrections 15 and 30 min after TPI (the flight plan, Table 1-6) [published]. The CSM state vector the ground uplinks with the CSI PAD is off by MSFN's tracking error, Apollo 11's [estimated]

lunar_orbit._comment: Apollo 12's lunar orbit after LOI-2, above the landing site's radius: 66.1 by 54.3 nmi, LOI-2 cutting off at 87:49:05 at 1.89 S 150.85 E, 61.7 nmi up and 0.30 deg climbing (MSC-01855, Tables 5-III and 5-VI) [published], its pericynthion 105 deg back along the orbit, about 103.7 W [derived]. The lunar_orbit start phase starts there, placed along the orbit for the flown undocking and DOI. LOI-2's PAD targets 66.2 by 54.1 nmi at 87:48:47.39, its N81 -139.2, +0.1, -89.5 up (Apollo Flight Journal, 86:12:07) [published]: burned there, the burn point on its way up from the new pericynthion, where the Moon's field rounds the orbit out toward the rendezvous. The SPS gave 950 m/s to here: MCC-2, LOI-1 and LOI-2 (61.8, 2,889.5 and 165.2 ft/s, MSC-01855, Tables 5-IV and 5-VI) [published]

tei._comment: TEI onto Apollo 12's return: 3,042.0 ft/s at 172:27:16.8 for 130.3 s (MSC-01855, Table 5-VIII) [published]; the TEI-45 PAD's TIG, 172:27:16.14, and N81 +3,027.2, +302.1, -25.3 ft/s, from which the RTCC starts its solve (Apollo Flight Journal, 171:04:49) [published]; entry interface came at 244:22:19.1, 13.80 S 173.52 E, 36,116 ft/s, 6.48 deg down, heading 98.16 deg east of north (ibid., Table 5-IX) [published]. That state, put in the simulator, is on a return inclined return_inclination_deg to the equator with its vacuum perigee entry_perigee_alt_km up (Rtcc.vacuum_perigee()) [derived]. The RTCC solves the burn for that inclination, that entry interface and that corridor (Rtcc.plan_tei()), near the flown TEI's time, where it needs no part up or down (tig_free): Apollo 12's N81 had 25.3 ft/s up, and the simulator's CSM comes round to the flown TEI's place minutes before its time [simplified]

entry._comment: Apollo 12's target, N61 in the final entry PAD at 239:31:59 (Apollo Flight Journal): 15.81 deg S, 165.17 deg W [published]. The ground uplinks it with the entry PAD (the timeline's entry_pad), and the entry start phase starts with it loaded

dispersions._comment: The seed the flight's dispersions are drawn from: the CSM's unmodelled forces (spacecraft.json "unmodelled"), once for the flight, and MSFN's tracking error ("msfn"), for each uplink

msfn._comment: The Manned Space Flight Network's tracking error in the CSM state vector the RTCC plans the CSM's PADs from and uplinks with them (P27): standard deviations in LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down), by the body the CSM's orbit is about, Apollo 11's [estimated]

timeline._comment: Mission Control from TLI to the entry. Each entry happens once: at its GET ('get'), or 's' seconds 'after' a mission event or a planned time, or 'before' a planned time (the sequencer's plan), if its condition ('when', a flight phase or one of the sequencer's) holds then; CAPCOM makes the call ('say') and the ground uplinks the PAD ('pad'): the RTCC's solution, a midcourse correction's at its TIG ('tig'), a plane change's or TEI's at the opportunity nearest 'near', or a maneuver the flight plan fixed ('n81_ft_s', LVLH) at 'tig'. The times, calls and PADs are Apollo 12's [published: the Apollo Flight Journal and Lunar Surface Journal: GO for TLI 2:28:15; the MCC-2 PAD 29:01:46; the final LOI-1 PAD 80:50:55; GO for LOI 83:02:58; the LOI-2 PAD 86:12:07; GO for LOI-2 87:14:11; the undocking and separation times 105:49:35, the separation 2.5 ft/s radially down (the flight plan, Table 1-5; its flight-path angle turned from -0.18 to -0.20 deg, MSC-01855, Table 5-III); GO for undocking 107:46:19; the DOI PAD 108:00:32, 6 min 30 s after undocking at 107:54:02.3; GO for DOI 108:53:24, 1,815 s before DOI; the PDI state vector 109:50:46, 1,792 s before PDI (110:20:37.58); GO for PDI 110:17:37; the landing site update, Noun 69, 110:21:57, 79 s after PDI; GO for enter 110:22:23; GO for landing 110:29:45; STAY for T1 110:34:44 and T3 111:37:49 after the landing at 110:32:36.2; the first plane change's PAD 118:01:54, TIG 119:47:12.54; the ascent PAD 140:19:25, TIG 142:03:47.00; GO to cast off 141:31:08; the CSI update 142:29:20, 1,109 s after the insertion; GO for Pyro Arm 147:42:29, 7,569 s after docking at 145:36:20.2; the second plane change's PAD 157:32:01; the TEI-45 PAD's update 171:04:49; the MCC-5 PAD 187:56:58; the MCC-7 PAD 239:24:55; the entry PAD 239:31:59; GO for Pyro Arm 243:27:16]. MCC-1 wasn't flown, and the first correction, MCC-2, took the stack off the free return. The flight's CSI PAD came before the liftoff; here the update after the insertion brings it [simplified]. undocking_get: the flown undocking, to which the LM's start phases fly docked

entries.say: Apollo 12, Houston. The good word is you're Go for TLI.

entries._estimated: the PAD's time, an hour before MCC-4's (the flight plan's 78:25:18.2, its nominal Delta-V zero, not flown): the RTCC here flies it when the tracking has left the approach off

entries.say: Hello, 12; Houston. You're Go for LOI.
Hello, Apollo 12; Houston. You're Go for LOI-2, and your PIPA's look real good.
Intrepid, Houston. You're Go for undocking.
Those are great. You're Go for DOI.
Intrepid; Houston. Go P00 and Data. We're ready to go.
Intrepid, Houston. You're stay for T1.
Intrepid, Houston. You're go to cast off on this Rev.
Intrepid, Houston. We have your CSI update. Over.
Yankee Clipper, Houston. Go for Pyro Arm.
12, Houston. You're Go for Pyro Arm.

start_notes.lunar_ascent: Intrepid 20 min before liftoff, the plane change flown
